harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Tailor your summary to each specific job application.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: A generic summary fails to demonstrate fit for the specific role.
examples: Replace generic phrases with keywords from the job description

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Keep your summary to 3-4 lines or 50-75 words.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: Recruiters spend an average of 7 seconds scanning a resume.
examples: Focus on your most relevant qualifications and career goals

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Lead with your strongest qualification or most relevant experience.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: The first impression should immediately demonstrate value.
examples: Start with years of experience, key achievement, or relevant certification

harvard_resume_rules.reason: Numbers provide concrete evidence of impact and improve credibility.
examples: Increased sales by 25% in Q3
Managed team of 8 engineers
Reduced processing time by 35%

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Start each bullet point with a strong action verb.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: Action verbs demonstrate initiative and make descriptions more dynamic.
examples: Spearheaded
Implemented
Optimized
Delivered
Negotiated

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Focus on results and impact rather than responsibilities.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: Employers want to see what you accomplished, not just what you were supposed to do.
examples: Instead of 'Responsible for sales', write 'Exceeded sales targets by 15% for 3 consecutive quarters'

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Prioritize experience most relevant to the target role.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: Relevant experience demonstrates immediate value to the employer.
examples: Move relevant roles higher, de-emphasize less relevant positions

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Include skills mentioned in the job description.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: ATS systems and recruiters look for keyword matches.
examples: Mirror the exact terminology used in the job posting

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Group skills by category for better readability.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: Organized skills are easier to scan and demonstrate breadth.
examples: Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript, SQL
Cloud: AWS, Azure

harvard_resume_rules.instruction: Include relevant coursework, projects, and achievements.
harvard_resume_rules.reason: Education details demonstrate knowledge and initiative.
examples: Relevant Coursework: Machine Learning, Data Structures
Senior Project: Built predictive model

mit_resume_rules.instruction: Use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
mit_resume_rules.reason: Structured bullets are easier to read and demonstrate clear impact.
examples: Situation: Legacy system slow
Task: Improve performance
Action: Refactored code
Result: 50% faster

mit_resume_rules.instruction: Include technical keywords relevant to the position.
mit_resume_rules.reason: Technical roles require specific skill demonstrations.
examples: Mention specific technologies, frameworks, and tools used

mit_resume_rules.instruction: Order skills by relevance to the target role.
mit_resume_rules.reason: Most relevant skills should be most visible.
examples: Put required skills first, then preferred skills

mit_resume_rules.instruction: Include project links and technologies used.
mit_resume_rules.reason: Projects demonstrate practical application of skills.
examples: GitHub link, technologies used, impact achieved

yale_resume_rules.instruction: Write in third person implied (no 'I' or 'my').
examples: Instead of 'I managed a team', write 'Managed team of 10'

yale_resume_rules.instruction: Demonstrate progression and growth in your career.
yale_resume_rules.reason: Shows ambition and capability for advancement.
examples: Promoted from Analyst to Senior Analyst within 18 months

ats_rules.instruction: Use standard section headings (Summary, Experience, Education, Skills).
ats_rules.reason: ATS systems parse standard headings to categorize content.
examples: Use 'Work Experience' instead of 'My Journey'

ats_rules.instruction: Avoid tables, columns, headers, and footers.
ats_rules.reason: ATS systems cannot parse complex formatting correctly.
examples: Use simple single-column layout

ats_rules.instruction: Use exact keywords from the job description.
ats_rules.reason: ATS systems score resumes based on keyword matches.
examples: If job says 'React', use 'React' not 'React.js' or 'ReactJS'

ats_rules.instruction: Include both acronyms and full terms.
ats_rules.reason: ATS may search for either form.
examples: Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
Project Management Professional (PMP)

ats_rules.reason: Non-standard fonts may not render correctly in ATS.
examples: Avoid decorative fonts like Comic Sans or Papyrus

ats_rules.instruction: Include job title keywords in your experience bullets.
ats_rules.reason: ATS scores experience sections for keyword relevance.
examples: If applying for 'Software Engineer', include 'software engineering' in bullets

internal_rules.instruction: Every experience bullet should contain at least one metric.
internal_rules.reason: Quantified achievements are 40% more likely to be remembered.
examples: Percentages, dollar amounts, time frames, team sizes, or counts

internal_rules.instruction: Summary must mention the target role or industry.
examples: Experienced software engineer seeking senior backend role

internal_rules.instruction: Skills section should have 10-15 relevant skills.
internal_rules.reason: Too few skills looks thin; too many looks unfocused.
examples: Group by category: Languages, Frameworks, Tools, Cloud

internal_rules.instruction: Address the hiring manager by name when possible.
internal_rules.reason: Personalization shows effort and attention to detail.
examples: Dear Hiring Manager is last resort; research the name

internal_rules.instruction: Connect your experience directly to the job requirements.
internal_rules.reason: Shows you understand the role and can deliver results.
examples: Your requirement for X aligns with my experience in Y
